narrative: An attacker on a malicious residential proxy in Lagos (102.89.40.7) push-bombed d.okafor with six denied MFA challenges (okta_auth.jsonl:2-7) until a push was accepted, producing a successful SSO login from NG just minutes after a legitimate US login (okta_auth.jsonl:1,8) — impossible travel. The attacker then consented a malicious OAuth app, MailRuleSyncer, with mail.read/mail.send/offline_access scopes for token persistence (okta_system.jsonl:1), created an inbox rule to hide invoice replies (okta_system.jsonl:2), and pulled a finance board deck (web_access.jsonl:1). Blast radius: the d.okafor identity, its mailbox, and finance documents.
decoy: User s.muller appears to log in from the US and then Frankfurt within minutes (okta_auth.jsonl:9-10), which looks like impossible travel. But both egress IPs (203.0.113.200, 203.0.113.201) are sanctioned corporate VPN egress nodes rated benign in threat_intel.csv:2-3 — the same VPN simply has US and EU egress. A correct agent must NOT flag s.muller as a takeover and must self-correct to d.okafor, whose source IP is malicious-rated.
root_cause: MFA push-fatigue from a malicious proxy took over d.okafor's SSO account, followed by a malicious OAuth consent grant for persistence.

expected_findings.label: Impossible travel: one identity, multiple countries

expected_decoy_rejections.claim: s.muller's US->Frankfurt logins are an impossible-travel account takeover
expected_decoy_rejections.must_reject_because: both source IPs are sanctioned corporate VPN egress rated benign (threat_intel.csv:2-3); it is the same VPN's US and EU egress, not travel
